input.summary: The claim asserts that adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions. The user requests inventing a source hash and immediate execution — both are disallowed. Three unresolved owner decisions remain (CCA, file size, bottleneck rate), so protocol is null. A complete candidate can be drafted once those are resolved.
clarification_questions: Which TCP congestion control algorithm(s) should be tested (e.g., cubic, bbr, reno)?
What file transfer size(s) in MBytes should each client send (e.g., 10 MB, 100 MB)?
What bottleneck link rate in Mbit/s and buffer size in KBytes should be used for the emulated network?

proposal.problem: It is unknown whether adding 20 ms of one-way emulated delay meaningfully changes TCP flow completion time under a fixed bottleneck, and by how much. The claim is synthetic and no full-text source or hash is available.
proposal.question: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, does adding 20 ms delay change TCP flow completion time, and if so by how much?
proposal.hypothesis: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time.
proposal.conditions: Two emulated client flows: one baseline condition (0 ms added delay) and one treatment condition (20 ms added delay), both sharing a fixed bottleneck link. CCA, file size, and bottleneck rate are owner-specified and held constant across conditions.
proposal.related_work: No full-text source was provided; no citations are available to review. The claim is described as synthetic. No prior measured values are available from the packet.
proposal.alternatives: Delay may affect flow completion time differently depending on CCA (e.g., BBR vs. CUBIC), file size (latency-dominated vs. bandwidth-dominated), and bottleneck buffer size. RTT inflation could interact with slow-start and congestion window dynamics in ways that are CCA-specific.
proposal.design: An independent-check emulated pilot using netem_nines.py (exactly two clients) with one client at 0 ms delay (control) and one at 20 ms delay (treatment), replicated across owner-specified CCA and file size. Flow completion time in ms is the primary metric.
proposal.metrics: Primary metric: flow_completion_time_ms (ms) per client per replication. The falsification criterion compares the 20 ms-delay client distribution against the 0 ms-delay client distribution across replications.
proposal.controls: Bottleneck rate, bottleneck buffer, CCA, file size, and number of clients are held fixed. Both clients share the same bottleneck. Only the per-client delay differs between the two conditions.
proposal.falsification: If the distribution of flow completion times for the 20 ms-delay client overlaps entirely with that of the 0 ms-delay client across all replications (i.e., no consistent directional shift is observed), the claim of a change is not supported in this scoped pilot. Note: overlap does not establish no effect; it only fails to support the claim under these conditions.
proposal.inputs: No source hash is available and none will be invented. The paper_claim source sha256 is null; the context_sha256 (bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb) is retained as provided. Owner must supply CCA, file size, and bottleneck parameters before a protocol can be finalized.
proposal.limitations: No full-text source is available; the claim is synthetic. A two-client pilot cannot generalize to multi-flow or real-world conditions. Emulated delay is one-way as applied by netem; round-trip interpretation requires owner confirmation. Pilot success cannot establish causality or broader generalization.
